articles.title: Madhya Pradesh Excise Department Shifts To E-Bank Guarantees After Fake FDR Scams, Tightens Liquor Shop Licence Process
articles.description: Madhya Pradesh's Excise Department has adopted electronic bank guarantees for liquor shop tenders following multiple fake fixed deposit receipt scams. Commissioner Deepak Saxena said the system prevents deposit duplication. The move follows alleged financial irregularities involving fabricated guarantees, including cases linked to ₹49 crore and ₹56 crore excise scams.

articles.title: Odisha Cabinet approves free textbooks for 28.7 lakh students, Rs 500-crore urban drainage scheme
articles.description: Bhubaneswar, Oct13 (PTI): The Odisha government on Tuesday approved free textbooks for around 28.7 lakh students of state-run schools, along with a Rs 500-crore programme to improve urban drainage and tackle flooding. The decisions were among 16 proposals approved at a Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi here. The proposals, relating to 11 departments, will be implemented soon, Chief Secretary Anu Garg told reporters after the meeting. The decision to provide free textbooks to more students comes amid a controversy over the supply of textbooks containing errors, with opposition parties demanding the resignation of School and Mass Education Minister Nityananda Gond. Garg said students of classes 9 and 10 in government and government-aided secondary schools, other than those covered under the existing SC and ST provisions, would now receive free textbooks. The scheme aims to ensure equitable access to quality education, reduce the financial burden on economically weaker families, improve enrolment in government schools, lower dropout rates and increase the transition from elementary to secondary education. Students belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes were already receiving free textbooks, she said. "The scheme will remain in force for five years, from 2025-26 to 2029-30, with a total estimated outlay of Rs 284.07 crore, covering a tentative 28.7 lakh beneficiaries," Garg said. The procurement of paper, printing, transportation and distribution of textbooks will be undertaken through a transparent and competitive process in accordance with the Odisha General Financial Rules and applicable procurement guidelines, she said. The School and Mass Education Department will put in place a mechanism to collect, verify and validate beneficiary data through field-level verification. It will also ensure that textbooks are printed and supplied to schools well before the commencement of each academic session, Garg said. Over 1,600 mistakes, including spelling errors and incorrect names of eminent personalities, were found in 55 textbooks supplied by the department. In another major decision, the Cabinet approved the Urban Storm Water Drainage Management and Improvement Programme (USWDMIP), with an outlay of Rs 500 crore from the state's own resources over a period of five years, from 2026-27 to 2030-31. The scheme will cover urban local bodies and selected block headquarters. The proposed interventions include desilting, construction of reinforced cement concrete stormwater drains, covering of drains, restoration of natural drainage channels and their linkage with suitable water bodies. The measures are aimed at improving the capacity and efficiency of urban drainage systems and reducing waterlogging and localised flooding, Garg said. The programme is also expected to promote groundwater recharge, improve public safety and environmental quality, and support climate-resilient urban development. The Cabinet also approved the establishment of a Disaster Recovery-cum-Data Centre at Keonjhar to ensure the uninterrupted functioning of critical government digital services during major disruptions, including earthquakes and cyclones. The Odisha State Data Centre in Bhubaneswar hosts critical government applications, databases and platforms supporting government-to-government, government-to-business and government-to-citizen services. The proposed facility at Keonjhar will serve as a disaster recovery centre, enabling the state to protect its data and maintain essential services in the event of a major disruption at the Bhubaneswar facility. "Both Keonjhar and Bhubaneswar are located in different seismic zones. If there is any damage in Bhubaneswar, data could remain safe at the Keonjhar centre," Garg said. The project will cost over Rs 176 crore, including capital expenditure of Rs 154 crore and operational expenditure of Rs 22.83 crore for five years. An amount of Rs 162.83 crore has been provided from the Fifth State Finance Commission grant-in-aid, she said. The state Cabinet also approved a tender worth Rs 105 crore for the construction of an in-stream water storage project on the Tel river at Tustapali village in Bolangir district. The project is expected to strengthen water security and help mitigate chronic water scarcity in the drought-prone district. Apart from these proposals, the Cabinet approved measures relating to the Fisheries and Animal Resources Development; Industries, Skill Development and Technical Education; Finance; Electronics and Information Technology; Agriculture and Farmers' Empowerment; Housing and Urban Development; Revenue and Disaster Management; Water Resources; and School and Mass Education departments. PTI AAM AAM MNB (This story is published as part of the auto-generated syndicate wire feed. No editing has been done in the headline or the body by ABP Live.)

articles.title: Thirty Nine-fold rise in procurement as National SC-ST hub expands support for small entrepreneurs
articles.description: The National SC-ST Hub is expanding support for entrepreneurs from Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe communities through training, finance, technology assistance and market access. The initiative has also recorded a sharp rise in government procurement from SC/ST-owned micro and small enterprises, with purchases increasing from Rs 99.37 crore in 2015-16 to Rs 4,013.42 crore in 2025-26. A push beyond financial assistance For a small business, getting access to finance is only one part of the challenge. Finding customers, understanding government procurement rules, meeting quality standards and competing for larger contracts can be equally difficult. The National SC-ST Hub, or NSSH, has been designed around this wider challenge. Launched on October 18, 2016, and implemented through the National Small Industries Corporation, or NSIC, the initiative seeks to strengthen the participation of SC/ST-owned enterprises in India’s MSME ecosystem. The scheme brings together several forms of support, including entrepreneurship development, mentoring, training, technology assistance, financial support and market linkages. One of its key areas of focus is government procurement, where small businesses can get opportunities to supply products and services to government departments and public sector enterprises. This approach is important because entering institutional markets can help small enterprises move beyond local customers and develop a more stable business base. More than 1.90 lakh beneficiaries assisted The reach of the programme has expanded considerably since its launch. As of July 31, 2026, the National SC-ST Hub had assisted 1,90,414 beneficiaries, while 54,499 candidates had been trained through various programmes. The increase in government procurement is another indication of the growing participation of SC/ST-owned enterprises. Procurement from SC/ST-owned micro and small enterprises increased nearly 39 times, rising from Rs 99.37 crore in 2015-16 to Rs 4,013.42 crore in 2025-26. During 2025-26 alone, procurement worth Rs 4,013.42 crore was recorded from 12,524 MSEs. Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Assam emerged as the five leading States under the initiative, reflecting the growing geographical spread of the programme. Training has also been increasingly connected with actual market opportunities. During 2025-26, 10,717 candidates were trained through 47 institutions across 27 States, including 24 Aspirational Districts. Women accounted for 55 per cent of those trained, making their participation an important feature of the programme. Training linked to real business opportunities The training programmes under NSSH are not limited to general lessons in entrepreneurship. Several courses are linked to areas where there are opportunities in public procurement and on platforms such as the Government e-Marketplace, or GeM. The areas covered include cafeteria management and food production, welding, CAD/CAM, laundry services, fashion designing and tailoring, as well as bamboo-based work. For entrepreneurs who may have technical skills but limited experience of dealing with government buyers, such training can be particularly useful. Understanding how to register on procurement platforms, participate in tenders, calculate competitive prices and meet quality requirements can be as important as having the ability to produce a particular product or provide a service. The focus on procurement-oriented training is therefore aimed at helping entrepreneurs convert their skills into actual business opportunities. Also Read: From emergency indictment to election commission: The Navin Chawla record that Congress would rather not discuss Capital subsidy to help enterprises expand Access to affordable capital remains one of the major challenges for micro and small enterprises. The National SC-ST Hub addresses this through the Special Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme, or SCLCSS. Under the scheme, eligible new and existing SC/ST-owned MSEs can receive a 25 per cent capital subsidy, subject to a maximum of Rs 25 lakh, for investment in plant, machinery and equipment financed through institutional credit. Between the launch of the scheme and March 2026, 3,160 MSEs received support amounting to Rs 356.10 crore. The assistance has extended across 233 districts in 27 States and Union Territories. For businesses looking to modernise their production facilities or increase capacity, such support can reduce the upfront financial pressure involved in purchasing machinery and equipment. Upgrading technology can also make it easier for small enterprises to meet the quality and production standards required for larger institutional orders. Creating opportunities through government procurement Public procurement is one of the most important components of the National SC-ST Hub. The Single Point Registration Scheme, or SPRS, enables eligible MSEs to register with NSIC and access government procurement opportunities. Registered enterprises receive benefits such as free tender sets and exemption from payment of Earnest Money Deposit, subject to applicable conditions. The wider Public Procurement Policy also provides a specific target for purchases from MSEs. Central Ministries, Departments and Central Public Sector Enterprises are required to procure 25 per cent of their annual purchases from MSEs. Within this overall target, 4 per cent of total procurement is earmarked for SC/ST-owned MSEs. This provides a defined opportunity for smaller enterprises to participate in the government purchasing system. For a growing business, securing a government contract can provide more than immediate revenue. It can help establish credibility, increase production and create a track record that can be useful when competing for future institutional contracts. Helping enterprises find wider markets Having a good product or service does not necessarily guarantee that customers will find a business. Marketing and visibility are therefore another important part of the NSSH framework. The Special Marketing Assistance Scheme, or SMAS, supports SC/ST enterprises through exhibitions, trade fairs, vendor development programmes, workshops and awareness campaigns. During 2025-26, the scheme facilitated the participation of 141 SC/ST MSEs in four domestic exhibitions. At the same time, 247 Special Vendor Development Programmes were organised with Central Public Sector Enterprises. The initiative also conducted 197 e-tendering workshops and 230 awareness workshops with CPSEs and government departments. These programmes give entrepreneurs an opportunity to understand procurement procedures while also connecting them with potential institutional buyers. For many small enterprises, direct interaction with government departments and public sector companies can help them understand what buyers are looking for and how their products or services can fit into existing procurement requirements. articles.title: NTPC Floats GeM Tender for Bulk Procurement of Sodium Hypochlorite
articles.description: NTPC Limited floats GeM bid for bulk procurement of Industrial Grade Sodium Hypochlorite across multiple power stations. Bid closes on 2 November 2026.
